transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer service, my name is Nathan. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Nathan. I'm calling to claim the broadband speed guarantee credit. My sync speed has stayed down at thirty-eight megabits for over three weeks, well below my forty-five megabit minimum guarantee!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can look at your broadband line profile, but first I need to complete security. Can you verify your full name and the first line of your address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Elena Rostova, 52 Orchard Way, Cambridge, CB4 2PZ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security PIN on your account, Elena?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is 7391.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. What kind of speeds have you been measuring over the past three weeks?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Between thirty-four and thirty-eight megabits every single day. I ran the official tests on my Lenovo laptop wired directly to port 1 of the router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And is that using our official S-Net desktop speed test tool or an unverified third-party website?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Using your official S-Net member portal test tool, and every test log has been saved under my account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me while I pull up the exchange line sync telemetry and your test records.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Elena. The line sync history shows an average sync rate of thirty-seven point eight megabits over the trailing twenty-one days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right! Which is seven megabits below the contractual forty-five megabit guarantee I was promised when I signed up! I work from home and my video calls constantly freeze!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Speed guarantees are handled by Openreach line engineering, so you'll have to take up any credit dispute with Openreach directly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't have a contract with Openreach, Nathan! I pay S-Net sixty pounds every month! S-Net gives the guarantee!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you actually bothered to read the minimum guaranteed speed clause in your terms, you'd know it allows a thirty-day cure window before compensation applies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That attitude is completely unacceptable! It has already been thirty days since I first flagged this with your web chat team on September eighteenth!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I said, the automated ticket only logged an Openreach DLM profile reset on the twenty-second.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The DLM reset did nothing! The line SNR margin is locked at nine decibels, which is capping the sync rate!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check what hardware you used for the speed logs. Which computer model were you using to run the speed test?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you earlier, it was my Lenovo laptop plugged in via Ethernet cable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously I have to confirm the test client details before applying billing credits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, but this delay is costing me freelance client work! I need this line stabilized today, it's driving me insane!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hold on while I check if your account qualifies for an automatic compensation payout. Bear with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we are on the line, what type of microfilter or master socket faceplate is installed at your property?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's the NTE5c master socket with the built-in pre-filtered faceplate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And the grey DSL cable runs directly from the router into that top socket without extension leads?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, direct into the socket with the short two-meter cable provided in the box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, avoiding telephone extension wiring is crucial for maintaining stable VDSL high frequencies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the Openreach engineer who installed it two years ago told me never to use extension cables.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any older dial-up alarms or Sky boxes plugged into secondary phone sockets around the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, we don't have any other telephony devices plugged in anywhere in the house.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures there is no internal bridge-tap reflection degrading the downstream carrier bands.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes sense. Glad the internal wiring is completely clean.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for bearing with me. Because the sync speed remained below forty-five megabits for thirty consecutive days, your account qualifies for an automatic service guarantee credit of thirty pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that thirty pounds be deducted from my upcoming invoice?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I have applied a thirty-pound credit adjustment directly to your billing balance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about fixing the line speed itself? I don't just want a credit, I need the speed I pay for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can trigger an automated port reset on the street cabinet DSLAM right now to force a lower target noise margin of six decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that drop the connection briefly?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the router DSL light will flash amber for approximately ninety seconds while the cabinet reprofiles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go ahead and run the reset then, I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Reset command dispatched. The line is resynchronizing now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The DSL light stopped flashing and is solid green now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the new sync rate on my exchange monitor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new sync speed has established at fifty-three point four megabits down, with a six decibel SNR margin.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me run a speed test on my laptop right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Speed test shows fifty-one megabits download and eleven megabits upload! That's so much better!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you confirm you see the thirty-pound credit showing on your online account overview as well, Elena?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking the billing tab now... Yes, thirty pounds credit applied today with reference CR-9021.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your contact mobile number on file, it's 07700 900518, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my mobile number.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the dispatch notes, the service address is 52 Orchard Way, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 52 Orchard Way.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband speed that you need help with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the speed is finally above the guarantee and the credit is on my account. That solves it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Elena, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Nathan.
